MCMC constructs a Markov chain with the target posterior as stationary distribution. Metropolis–Hastings accepts/rejects proposals; HMC uses gradients and simulated trajectories; NUTS adapts trajectory length to reduce manual tuning. Samples can represent complex uncertainty, but autocorrelation, poor mixing, and multimodality require diagnostics such as effective sample size and multiple-chain convergence checks. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

VI optimizes a tractable distribution, commonly minimizing $D_{KL}(q\|p)$ through an ELBO. It scales well with stochastic optimization and amortized inference, but the chosen family and objective can miss modes or underestimate uncertainty. Compare predictive calibration, posterior-sensitive decisions, compute, and diagnostics rather than declaring one universally superior. MCMC is asymptotically principled under conditions; finite chains are not automatically exact, and a high ELBO does not establish a good approximation everywhere.
